body:
CliMA/ClimaAtmos.jl#4949 stretches vertical grids with ClimaCore's two-scale `BoundaryLayerHyperbolicTangentStretching`. The rule admits a range of `z_elem` set by `dz_bottom`, `dz_top` (3000 m by default), `z_pbl` (2200 m), and `z_max`, and building the grid throws an `ArgumentError` outside it. The downstream ClimaCoupler job on that PR fails for this reason in `climaatmos_coarse_short.yml`.

This PR sets `dz_top` in the 17 configs whose grids fall outside the range for the default `dz_top`. Each value lies just above the top spacing the single-scale stretching gives the grid, so the grids stay close to their current spacing:

| Grid | Configs | `dz_top` | Admissible range |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 levels to 30 km, `dz_bottom` 500 m | 8 `ci_configs`, `cmip_coarse` | 6350 m | 6280–6840 m |
| 39 levels to 60 km, 100 m | `cmip_oceananigans_climaseaice`, `_bucket` | 4050 m | 4000–5520 m |
| 70 levels to 70 km, 30 m | `wxquest_progedmf` | 3100 m | ≥ 3040 m |
| 130 levels to 70 km, 30 m | `weatherbench_progedmf_0m`, `_1m` | 1500 m | 1440–2000 m |
| 31 levels to 50 km, 100 m | `amip_test` | 4300 m | 4240–8180 m |
| 39 levels to 55 km, 30 m | `climaatmos_coarse_short` | 4650 m | ≥ 4600 m |
| 16 levels to 50 km, 100 m | `restart_cmip` | 9600 m | ≥ 9540 m |

Each config, merged with the ClimaAtmos defaults and its `atmos_config_file` as ClimaCoupler merges them, builds its grid with ClimaCore 1.0.8 in Float32 and Float64. The `test/config/input_test_*` files are only parsed and keep the default grid.

ClimaAtmos versions without the two-scale stretching ignore `dz_top` (with an "unused keys" warning), so this PR can merge before CliMA/ClimaAtmos.jl#4949 and changes no results until ClimaCoupler picks up a ClimaAtmos release that has it.
title: Set dz_top for grids the two-scale stretching rejects

body: ### Problem Currently, the ClimaCore extension in ConservativeRegridding only considers global transfers between FV and SE spaces. Since the ocean is not defined on the whole sphere, what we really need is a way to handle masked transfers. Using the same method as the global transfer fails because the scatter from the intersection grid divides each node's flux by its wet coverage, and with the sign-indefinite Lagrange basis (the $\phi$'s in the figure below) that coverage can be near zero or negative, so the normalized flux blows up. **Figure:** (a) One spectral element in reference coordinates, with GLL nodes (dots), control volumes (dashed), FV cells (thin lines) and dry cells (gray). The polygon $\Omega_k \cap \Omega_e$ (blue) overlaps several control volumes; its weight is the area of the hatched part. (b) The first two Lagrange basis functions for $N_q = 4$ (solid) take negative values (shaded), while the subcell indicators (dashed) are non-negative. Dotted lines mark the subcell edges $\zeta_i$. ### Solution #2116 fixed the issue with a clamp, but this broke conservation. In the present PR, we implement a cleaner fix by using a different basis, defined by piecewise constants on control volumes around each SE node (the $\psi$'s in the figure). The weights are nonnegative, so every node's coverage is in [0, 1]. The control volume areas are designed to equal the quadrature weights, so the scattered flux conserves the polygon flux integral. In this PR: - New `ext/ClimaCouplerCMIPExt/subcell_weights.jl` builds the control volumes and their weights. - For now: the scatter uses the control-volume weights and the gather keeps the SEM basis weights, so the two are built separately. - Removed the flux clamp from #2116 and `cov_cutoff` from #2051. - Updated tests, `docs/src/exchange_grid.md`, and `NEWS.md`. ### Future work: - Transfer downward radiation and precipitation with the transpose of the control-volume weights so they are consistent with the area fractions - Transfer the surface temperature to the atmosphere as emitted longwave (εσT⁴) with the control-volume weights, and recover T from it - Higher-order control volume basis - Move control volume code to ConservativeRegridding
title: Use control volumes for FV to SE exchange (1/4)
